# Security Policies and Procedures

This document outlines security procedures and general policies for the Express
project.

  * [Reporting a Bug](#reporting-a-bug)
  * [Disclosure Policy](#disclosure-policy)
  * [Receiving Security Updates](#receiving-security-updates)
  * [Comments on this Policy](#comments-on-this-policy)

## Reporting a Bug

The Express team and community take all security bugs in Express seriously.
Thank you for improving the security of Express. We appreciate your efforts and
responsible disclosure and will make every effort to acknowledge your
contributions.

Report security bugs by emailing the lead maintainer in the Readme.md file.

The lead maintainer will acknowledge your email within 48 hours, and will send a
more detailed response within 48 hours indicating the next steps in handling
your report. After the initial reply to your report, the security team will
endeavor to keep you informed of the progress towards a fix and full
announcement, and may ask for additional information or guidance.

Report security bugs in third-party modules to the person or team maintaining
the module. You can also report a vulnerability through the
[Node Security Project](https://nodesecurity.io/report).

## Disclosure Policy

When the security team receives a security bug report, they will assign it to a
primary handler. This person will coordinate the fix and release process,
involving the following steps:

  * Confirm the problem and determine the affected versions.
  * Audit code to find any potential similar problems.
  * Prepare fixes for all releases still under maintenance. These fixes will be
    released as fast as possible to npm.

## Comments on this Policy

If you have suggestions on how this process could be improved please submit a
pull request.

WORKDIR /app/pdf-test

# Create a simple test script that demonstrates the issue and solution
RUN echo 'const express = require("../");\n\
const http = require("http");\n\
const { URL } = require("url");\n\
const fs = require("fs");\n\
\n\
// Create sample PDF server\n\
const pdfServer = express();\n\
pdfServer.get("/sample.pdf", (req, res) => {\n\
  // Send a sample PDF file\n\
  res.set("Content-Type", "application/pdf");\n\
  // Using a buffer for binary data\n\
  const samplePdf = Buffer.from("PDF sample content", "binary");\n\
  res.send(samplePdf);\n\
});\n\
\n\
// Create proxy server that will fetch and serve the PDF\n\
const app = express();\n\
\n\
// Incorrect way - leading to blank PDF\n\
app.get("/incorrect-pdf", (req, res) => {\n\
  const url = "http://localhost:3001/sample.pdf";\n\
  const urlObj = new URL(url);\n\
  const options = {\n\
    host: urlObj.host,\n\
    path: urlObj.pathname + urlObj.search,\n\
    headers: {}\n\
  };\n\
  \n\
  http.get(options, function(response) {\n\
    let body = "";\n\
    response.on("data", function(data) {\n\
      body += data;\n\
    });\n\
    \n\
    response.on("end", function() {\n\
      res.set("Content-Type", "application/pdf");\n\
      res.send(new Buffer(body, "binary")); // This causes blank PDF\n\
    });\n\
  });\n\
});\n\
\n\
// Correct way - properly handling binary data\n\
app.get("/correct-pdf", (req, res) => {\n\
  const url = "http://localhost:3001/sample.pdf";\n\
  const urlObj = new URL(url);\n\
  const options = {\n\
    host: urlObj.host,\n\
    path: urlObj.pathname + urlObj.search,\n\
    headers: {}\n\
  };\n\
  \n\
  http.get(options, function(response) {\n\
    const chunks = [];\n\
    response.on("data", function(chunk) {\n\
      chunks.push(chunk);\n\
    });\n\
    \n\
    response.on("end", function() {\n\
      const buffer = Buffer.concat(chunks);\n\
      res.set("Content-Type", "application/pdf");\n\
      res.send(buffer); // Correctly handles binary data\n\
    });\n\
  });\n\
});\n\
\n\
// Start servers\n\
const pdfServerInstance = pdfServer.listen(3001, () => {\n\
  console.log("PDF server listening on port 3001");\n\
});\n\
\n\
const appInstance = app.listen(3000, () => {\n\
  console.log("App listening on port 3000");\n\
  console.log("Test incorrect PDF: http://localhost:3000/incorrect-pdf");\n\
  console.log("Test correct PDF: http://localhost:3000/correct-pdf");\n\
});\n' > pdf-test.js

\n\
This test demonstrates the issue with serving PDFs in Express as described in issue #2910.\n\
\n\
## Problem\n\
When binary data like PDFs are fetched from another service and served through Express,\n\
concatenating the data as strings can corrupt the binary data, resulting in blank PDFs.\n\
\n\
## Solution\n\
The correct approach is to collect binary data in chunks and use Buffer.concat() to\n\
properly handle the binary data.\n\
\n\
## Test endpoints\n\
- http://localhost:3000/incorrect-pdf - Shows the issue (blank PDF)\n\
- http://localhost:3000/correct-pdf - Shows the solution (working PDF)\n\
\n\
